newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-RAMPANT SAO PAULO HIT EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAMPANT SAO PAULO HIT EIGHT.

text.p: Rampant Sao Paulo blasted eight goals past hapless neighbours Juventus in a Sao Paulo championship match on Sunday.

Colombian striker Victor Aristizabal and new find Dodo both scored hat-tricks in their 8-1 win. Dodo, who at 22 has already played for several clubs, began the season on the substitutes' bench but has since fought his way into the team.
The result kept Sao Paulo second in group two and increased the gap between them and the third-placed team to five points.

Sao Paulo, who dominated South American club soccer in the early 1990s when they won two Libertadores Cup titles, have faded recently after being forced to spend millions on improving their huge Morumbi stadium.
Last year, they sacked Brazil's 1994 World Cup coach Carlos Alberto Parreira after a series of bad results and this month his replacement Muricy Ramalho was also dismissed.
Corinthians, who drew 1-1 with Portuguesa, lead the group a further five points ahead of Sao Paulo. Midfielder Marcelinho Carioca converted a free kick to score his 100th goal for the club.
With five matches each to play, both teams look set to reach the tournament's play-off.

The top two teams in each of the two groups qualify for the play-off stage of the competition. Under the rather complicated rules, the groups cross in the second half of the qualifying stage with teams in group one meeting those in group two.
Palmeiras, hammered 5-2 by arch-rivals Corinthians last week, beat Portuguesa Santista 4-1 away to increase their lead in group one to six points. Striker Luizao scored twice to take his tally to 14.
Portuguesa and Santos are battling for second place in the group. Santos drew 1-1 with Uniao Sao Joao to stay two points behind Portuguesa.

Botafogo stayed top of the second stage of the Rio de Janeiro championship by beating Vasco da Gama 1-0 while Romario was among Flamengo's goalscorers in their 3-0 win over Americano. It was his 18th goal of the tournament.
Botafogo, who also won the first stage, need a draw in their last game against second-placed Fluminense next week to win the second stage. Fluminense, one point behind, need to win.

The winners of the first, second and third stages go into the play-off but if Botafogo win more than one stage, they gain a huge advantage over their opponents in the final. If they win all three stages, they take the title automatically.
Flamengo are out of the second stage reckoning and will have to try their luck again in stage three.
